volcanes.texto: The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported an increase in low-level eruptive activity at Krakatau starting in early October. During 21 September-9 October seismicity indicating both shallow and deep magmatic processes did not significantly increase. Minor white-to-black ash plumes were occasionally visible in webcam images rising as high as 50 m above the crater, though weather conditions sometimes prevented views. The Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC) reported that ash plumes from Manam rose to 2.1 km (7,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted E, NE, N, and NW during 8-9 and 11-13 October.

The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Marapi (on Sumatra) continued during 8-14 October. An eruptive event was recorded at 0002 on 13 October by the seismic network but not visually observed due to weather conditions. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay 3 km away from the active crater.

The Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería (SERNAGEOMIN) and the Servicio Geológico Minero Argentino (SEGEMAR) reported that eruptive activity at Nevados de Chillán was ongoing in mid-October. A new lava flow was first visible at the summit of Nuevo volcano on 29 September and traveled SW. During a field visit on 1 October scientists observed the ejection of meter-sized blocks as high as 500 m above the summit and outward as far as 250 m. The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Minamidake Crater (Aira Caldera?s Sakurajima volcano) during 5-12 October. Crater incandescence was visible in nighttime webcam images during 5-9 October. A total of 15 eruptive events during 5-8 October produced ash plumes that rose 1-1.6 km above the crater and drifted in various directions. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a 5-level scale), and the public was warned to be cautious within 1 km of both the Minimadake and Showa craters.

The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported that effusive activity at Bezymianny continued during 8-14 October. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on most days; the volcano was occasionally obscured by weather clouds. Dates and times are provided in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC); events are in local time only where specified.

The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that eruptive activity at Dukono continued during 8-14 October, though hazy conditions prevented visual observations. Eruptive events were recorded by the seismic network during 8 and 10-12 October. Faint rumbling was heard at the Dukono observation post (11 km N) on 10 October. The Alert Level remained at Level 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay 4 km away from the Malupang Warirang Crater.

The Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV) reported that eruptive activity at Etna?s summit craters during 5-11 October was characterized by gas emissions at the summit craters and periodic minor ash emissions at Northeast Crater (NEC). Adverse weather conditions often prevented visual observations. The volcano Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) according to the Dipartimento della Protezione Civile.

The Instituto Nacional de Sismología, Vulcanologia, Meteorologia e Hidrología (INSIVUMEH) reported that eruptive activity at Fuego continued during 6-14 October. Daily explosions recorded by the seismic network, at rates of 2-8 per hour, generated gas-and-ash plumes that rose as high as 1.1 km above the summit and mainly drifted as far as 40 km in various directions. Shock waves and rumbling sounds from explosions were reported almost daily. Explosions also often ejected incandescent material, sometimes as high as 300 m above the summit, and onto the flanks causing incandescent block avalanche

The Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO) reported that slow lava effusion continued to feed a thick flow in Great Sitkin?s summit crater that advanced SE during 7-14 October based on webcam and satellite images. Minor earthquakes consistent with the growth of the lava dome and occasional rockfalls were detected by the seismic network. Weather clouds obscured webcam and satellite views during most of the week, though elevated surface temperatures were identified in satellite images during 7-8 October. The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Ibu continued during 1-7 October, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Daily gray or white-to-gray ash plumes rose 200-800 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the public was advised to stay 2 km away from the active crater and 3.5 km away from the N crater wall opening.

The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported continuing eruptive activity at Kanlaon during 7-14 October. The seismic network recorded 0-19 daily volcanic earthquakes and during 11-13 October 5-6 daily periods of volcanic tremor lasting 2-64 minutes. In general, sulfur dioxide emissions ranged from 932 to 3,219 tonnes per day (t/d), though a peak of 4,656 t/d was recorded on 10 October, the same day as a larger eruptive event. The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the eruption at Karangetang?s North Crater (Kawah Dua) continued during 8-14 October. White plumes rose as high as 20 m above the summit and drifted in various directions on most days. At 1402 on 11 October a white-and-gray ash plume rose 700 m above the summit and drifted W and NW. Nearly an hour later, at 1459, a white, gray, and brown ash plume rose 700 m above the summit and drifted W and NW. Faint rumbling was heard on 12 October, though no emissions were recorded. The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by incandescence, intermittent spatter, and lava flows from vents along the SW and W margins of Halema`um`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 7-14 October. Incandescence and flaming continued to be visible at the N and S vents during 6-11 October, with periodic spattering at the N vent. Robust volcanic gas plumes rose from both vents in daytime webcam views. Several small lava overflows from a small vent at the base of N vent were observed during 9-10 October. Th

The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported continuing eruptive activity at Lewotolok during 8-14 October. On 8 and 11 October dense gray ash plumes rose around 500 m above the summit and drifted W and NW, and white steam-and-gas plumes rose 100 m above the summit and also drifted W and NW on 9, 12, and 14 October; no emissions were recorded on 10 and 13 October. Active lava flows on the S and SE flanks were 400-600 m long. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4). The public was warned to stay 2 km away from the summit with an extension to 3 km on the S and SE

The Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) reported that on 9 October ash plumes from Masaya were visible in webcam images rising to 1.2-1.5 km (4,000-5,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifting SW and W. Weather clouds blocked satellite views.

The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Mayon during 7-14 October. The seismic network recorded 6-14 daily volcanic earthquakes. Sulfur dioxide emissions generally averaged 905-1,474 tonnes per day. Daily emissions rose 100-900 m above the crater and drifted WNW, WSW, and SW. Minor Strombolian activity at 0318 on 11 October generated an ash plume that rose 500 m above the summit and drifted WNW. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a 0-5 scale) and the public was reminded to stay away from the 6-km-radius Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ).

The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the eruption at Merapi (on Java) continued during 8-14 October with avalanches produced by the active lava dome on the upper SW flank. The seismic network recorded multiple lava avalanches per day on most days that traveled as far as 2 km down the Sat/Putih, Bebeng, and Krasak drainages on the SW flank and the Boyong drainage on the S flank. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4), and the public was warned to stay 3-7 km away from the summit, based on location.

The Centro Nacional de Prevención de Desastres (CENAPRED) reported that eruptive activity was low at Popocatépetl during 7-14 October. The seismic network recorded 19-42 long-period events per day, accompanied by steam-and-gas emissions that drifted in multiple directions; the emissions contained small amounts of ash on a few of the days. The seismic network also detected one volcano-tectonic earthquake per day on 9, 11, and 13 October. The Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) reported that during 8-14 October daily ash plumes from Puracé rose to 5.1-6.1 km (17,000-20,000 ft) a.s.l., or as high as 1.4 km above the summit, and drifted NW, WNW, and SW based on webcam images, satellite images, weather models, and Volcano Observatory Notices to Aviation issued by the Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC). Emissions on 13 October were considered likely, but were not detected due to weather conditions. The Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-color scale).

The Instituto Geofísico del Perú?s (IGP) Centro Vulcanológico Nacional (CENVUL) reported continuing eruptive activity at Sabancaya during 5-11 October. The seismic network detected 18 seismic events associated with the movement of magmatic fluids, along with earthquakes indicating internal rock fracturing; no volcanic explosions occurred during the period. Gas, steam, and ash emissions periodically rose as high as 800 m above the summit and drifted less than 10 km NE and E. The Instituto Nacional de Sismología, Vulcanología, Meteorología e Hidrología (INSIVUMEH) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Santa Maria?s Santiaguito dome complex during 7-14 October, with continuing lava extrusion at Caliente dome. Incandescence at the summit was observed during dark hours. Effusion of blocky lava and collapses of material produced daily incandescent block avalanches that descended the flanks, particularly the W, SW, and S flanks; during 7-8 and 11-12 October these collapses generated short pyroclastic flows that reached the base on the cone. The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity continued at Semeru during 8-14 October, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. White-to-gray or gray ash plumes rose 300-1,000 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions on most days; emissions were not visible due to weather conditions on 8 and 10 October. The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported continuing lava effusion and explosive activity at the lava domes along the N crater floor of Young Sheveluch (on the SW flank of Old Sheveluch) during 7-14 October. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on a few of the days; weather clouds occasionally obscured views. The Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the second highest level on a four-color scale). Dates are based on UTC; specific events are in local time where noted.

The Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV) reported that eruptive activity continued at Stromboli during 5-11 October. Webcam images showed Strombolian activity from vents in Area N within the upper part of the Sciara del Fuoco, and vents in Area C-S (South-Central Crater) on the crater terrace. Explosions at Area N ejected lapilli and bombs above the vents and explosions at Area C-S ejected both fine and coarse tephra above the vents. The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that eruptive activity at Suwanosejima's Ontake Crater during 7-8 October produced ash plumes that rose as high as 400 m above the crater rim. The activity was the first recorded since 25 July. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second level on a five-level scale) and the public was warned to be cautious within 1.5 km of the crater.

The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported eruptive activity at Taal during 6-12 October. The seismic network recorded 0-34 daily volcanic earthquakes, including 1-9 periods of volcanic tremor each day during 7-10 October, with periods lasting between 2 and 82 minutes. Daily gas-and-steam emissions generally rose 600-1,500 m above the crater rim and drifted W, SW, and SE. Sulfur dioxide emissions averaged 952-3,071 tonnes per day during 6 and 8-10 October.
